turn_text: Welcome to the first five, a podcast of the Freedom Forum Institute in Washington, D.C., dedicated to exploring issues and news around the five freedoms of the First Amendment. I'm your host, Gene Polisinski. We're joined today by Congressman Mark Dishonier of California's 11th District, which is just east of San Francisco, I believe. He's introduced the Saving Local News Act, a bill aimed at helping newspapers survive by making it easier for them to become nonprofit organizations. We've reached Representative Dissonier by phone on Capitol Hill. Congressman, thanks for joining us today.
My pleasure. Thanks for inviting me.
We can guess the gist of your bill, of course, by its name, but explain what it specifically would do and why it's needed, if you would.

Well, this is one bill of a number of initiatives that I've been involved with trying to restore the health of local journalism in particular, which we've seen dramatically reduced as newsprint has changed to digital and as concentrations of ownership has happened. So this bill would just make it easier. Right now if you want to do a non-profit for news digitally or in print, like as they have in Philadelphia, you have to get the IRS to approve that based on its educational purpose. This having worked with the newspaper industry. makes it easier. It says that if you made the guidelines of providing local journalism, then basically you will have nonprofit status conferred on you. And then secondarily, and this is important for the sustainability of the model, it allows you not to be taxed on your advertising.
